description: Atlassian provides collaboration and software-development tools such as Jira and Confluence for project management, knowledge sharing, and DevOps.
description_cn: 提供 Jira、Confluence 等团队协作与软件研发工具，用于项目管理、知识沉淀和 DevOps 协作。

tools.description: Get current user info
tools.name: atlassianUserInfo

tools.description: Get cloudId to make tool calls. When a link is provided (e.g. [REDACTED] try passing the site hostname (e.g. site.atlassian.net) as cloudId to other tools first; if that fails, use this tool to list accessible resources.
tools.name: getAccessibleAtlassianResources

tools.description: Get the canonical Confluence HTML-format guidance for `createConfluencePage` or `updateConfluencePage`. Use this tool before authoring HTML/default page bodies or fine-grained HTML edits. First call with only `toolName`; if the returned guidance references a follow-up document, call this tool again with the same `toolName` and `reference` set to that single referenced path. Fetch one document per call. Valid `toolName` values: createConfluencePage, updateConfluencePage.
tools.name: getContentFormatGuide

tools.description: Get a Confluence page or blog post by ID, including body content. Use getTeamworkGraphContext with objectType ConfluencePage, ConfluenceBlogPost, ConfluenceWhiteboard, or ConfluenceSpace to get linked comments, child pages, shared users, and page owners.
tools.name: getConfluencePage

tools.description: Search Confluence content (pages, blog posts, comments, attachments) using CQL (Confluence Query Language). CQL is specific to Confluence and is not interchangeable with JQL.
tools.name: searchConfluenceUsingCql

tools.description: Get spaces
tools.name: getConfluenceSpaces

tools.description: Get pages or blog posts in a space
tools.name: getPagesInConfluenceSpace

tools.description: Get footer comments for a page or blog post
tools.name: getConfluencePageFooterComments

tools.description: Get inline comments for a page or blog post
tools.name: getConfluencePageInlineComments

tools.description: Get reply(child) comments for a comment
tools.name: getConfluenceCommentChildren

tools.description: Get child pages of specified page
tools.name: getConfluencePageDescendants

tools.description: Create a Confluence page, live doc, or blog post. Prefer live docs for page/doc requests (contentType="page", subtype="live"). Use classic pages for explicit requests, space requirements, knowledge bases/customer-facing help, or page-only workflows such as unpublished drafts. When contentFormat is "html" or omitted because HTML is the default, first call the getContentFormatGuide tool with { toolName: "createConfluencePage" } and follow the returned HTML-format guidance. Do not call it when contentFormat is "markdown".
tools.name: createConfluencePage

tools.description: Update a Confluence page or blog post. When contentFormat is "html" or omitted because HTML is the default, first call the getContentFormatGuide tool with { toolName: "updateConfluencePage" } and follow the returned HTML-format guidance. Do not call it when contentFormat is "markdown".
tools.name: updateConfluencePage

tools.description: Create a footer comment on a page or blog post
tools.name: createConfluenceFooterComment

tools.description: Create an inline comment on specific text in a page or blog post. For top-level comments, provide pageId and inlineCommentProperties (text selection + match counts). For replies, provide parentCommentId only (no pageId or inlineCommentProperties). You must first fetch the page content (e.g. using getConfluencePage) to find the exact text and count how many times it appears. Incorrect or missing inlineCommentProperties can result in a 400 error from the Confluence API.
tools.name: createConfluenceInlineComment

Use getJiraIssue with fields ["*all"] or a custom list if you need more.

tools.description: Create a Jira issue. Use additional_fields to set any Jira field that does not have its own parameter (e.g. custom fields, priority, components).

tools.description:
Retrieves connected context from Teamwork Graph for any Atlassian entity. Returns all relationships and linked objects within one traversal – including cross-product and third-party connections. Use when the answer requires connections between entities, not just a single entity's fields.

Supported entry points:

Jira: issues, projects, sprints, versions, comments

Confluence: pages, blogposts, whiteboards, databases, spaces

Goals, Projects, Focus Areas, Tags and updates

People: users, teams, organisations

DevOps: PRs, repos, deployments, services, builds, designs

Loom: videos, meetings

Compass: components

Assets: objects

Incidents, conversations, calendar events, external documents

After calling this tool, call getTeamworkGraphObject on returned ARIs to get full content.

The utilisation of this tool may consume up to 10 Rovo Credits. If the user or organization does not have any Rovo Credits available, the tool call will fail.
tools.name: getTeamworkGraphContext

tools.description: Fetches the entire available data for one or more objects (Atlassian or third-party) using their ARIs or URLs. Use for the objects gathered from getTeamworkGraphContext tool.
tools.name: getTeamworkGraphObject

tools.description: Adds a relationship between two entities in the Teamwork Graph (e.g. linking two Jira work items, marking one as blocking another, attaching a remote link, or connecting a Jira work item to an Atlas project or goal).
tools.name: addTeamworkGraphContext

tools.description: Search Jira, Confluence and linked 3P data using Rovo Search, ALWAYS use this tool to search for Jira and Confluence content unless the word CQL or JQL is used in the context. The utilisation of this tool may consume up to 10 Rovo Credits. If the user or organization does not have any Rovo Credits available, the tool call will fail.
tools.name: search

tools.description: Get a Jira issue or Confluence page by its ARI (Atlassian Resource Identifier). Only call this tool if your id is an ARI of the form "ari:cloud:jira:{cloudId}:issue/{id}" or "ari:cloud:confluence:{cloudId}:page/{id}". If it is not, do not call this tool — use another tool that accepts the identifier you have
tools.name: fetch
